rendered: The review does not recommend this. It presents dissolving aluminium foil in an alkaline solution as a poor option. The stated reason is sustainability: recovering the current collectors matters because copper smelting is a major source of emissions in the battery life cycle, so dissolving Al in alkaline solution is judged "not a sustainable separation method". [1][2][3] The review instead points to methods that separate the cathode coating from the Al foil without dissolving the foil, such as ethylene glycol, which can delaminate cathode films from Al foil in seconds without corroding the foil, though it notes that PVDF binder is not removed by that approach.
